You got it pretty right. I've a web programmer friend who I've done freelance work for, and between the jobs she and I have had creating intranets, bulletin boards, social communities... Basic approach is, everything gets thrown into a main channel, and the people congregate there--if the site is successful, the diversity of that main channel will then spill over into subforums, and so on. I've found that starting a bulletin board with a ton of different forums/subcategories can fail because there isn't a user population sufficient to populate them. It's like putting a bunch of sea monkeys into a bucket, and watching the bucket fill, and only after the main larger bucket is full enough do the sea monkeys spill into the smaller surrounding buckets. We are all sea monkeys in a larger ocean.
